title: Teller turnover surge at Cedar Hollow Bank

organization.size: 1,350 employees, 46 branches in four regions, average teller headcount 412, $6.8B in assets

presentingRequest: Branch teller turnover went from 28% to 47% in a single fiscal year. Our tellers are leaving for the credit unions and the big-box stores because we don't pay enough - the exit surveys say pay is the number-one reason. I want a 15% across-the-board teller pay increase approved before the FY2027 budget locks on December 10. Karen Lindgren also wants the branch managers with the worst turnover held accountable, and I'm inclined to support that as well. Please confirm the diagnosis and give us a recommendation we can take to the board's compensation committee. - Patricia Neumann, Chief Operating Officer

evidence.text: "This is a pay problem, full stop. Lakeshore Federal Credit Union across the street from our Main & 3rd branch pays at least two dollars an hour more. Every branch manager I talk to tells me the same thing. The exit surveys put pay at the top of the list. We haven't done anything else differently - the job is the same job it was two years ago. If we don't move on pay before the budget locks, we lose another year."

evidence.source: HR Analytics, teller turnover report FY2025 vs FY2026 (fiscal year Oct-Sep), reconciled to payroll final-pay records, 2026-10-20
evidence.text: Teller job family (Teller I, Teller II, Head Teller), average headcount 412 in both years. FY2025: 115 separations (98 voluntary, 17 involuntary) = 27.9%. FY2026: 193 separations (171 voluntary, 22 involuntary) = 46.8%. Reconciliation note: the HRIS moved from the legacy system to PeopleCore in December 2025. Both years count terminations of employment only; internal transfers and promotions are coded separately and excluded in both years. FY2025 count (legacy) matches 115 payroll final-pay records; FY2026 count (PeopleCore) matches 193 payroll final-pay records. Leavers with under 12 months' tenure: 41% of FY2025 leavers, 58% of FY2026 leavers. Report is firm-wide by job code only; no breakdown by branch, region or manager was produced.

evidence.source: HR Analytics, monthly voluntary teller separations, FY2025 and FY2026
evidence.text: FY2025: Oct-Mar total 43 (avg 7.2/month); Apr-Sep total 55 (avg 9.2/month). FY2026: Oct 11, Nov 10, Dec 12, Jan 11, Feb 11 (Oct-Feb total 55, avg 11.0/month); Mar 16; Apr 17, May 18, Jun 16, Jul 17, Aug 17, Sep 15 (Apr-Sep total 100, avg 16.7/month). FY2026 total 171.

evidence.source: HR, exit survey summaries FY2025 and FY2026 (emailed to voluntary leavers 2 weeks after last day; reasons are multi-select)
evidence.text: FY2026: 33 of 171 voluntary leavers responded (19%). Reasons: pay 20 (61%); schedule/hours 16 (48%); relationship with manager 12 (36%); career growth 10 (30%). Branch was optional and given by 31 respondents: 16 from ShiftWise branches, 15 from other branches. Of the 16 citing schedule/hours, 8 named a ShiftWise branch, 7 another branch, 1 no branch. FY2025: 26 of 98 responded (27%). Reasons: pay 15 (58%); schedule/hours 5 (19%); career growth 8 (31%); other 6 (23%). Instrument note: the 'relationship with manager' option was added in January 2026; the FY2025 survey had no manager option.

Last external market study: Brightline Rewards, May 2023, placed the Teller I midpoint ($17.10/hour) at the 51st percentile of the bank's labor markets. No market study since. Structure adjustments: 3.0% (Jan 2024), 3.0% (Jan 2025), 2.5% (Jan 2026). Current Teller I starting rate $17.60/hour, midpoint $18.65/hour. 'We do not know where we sit against the market today. The State Bankers Association sells its 2026 teller pay module separately; we did not buy it this year.'

evidence.source: Talent Acquisition recruiter, local job-posting scan (email, 2026-10-14)
evidence.text: Six postings 'that candidates have mentioned to me': Lakeshore FCU full-time teller $19.50; Ridgeway Credit Union full-time member service rep $19.00; Atlas National Bank universal banker (requires securities licensing) $20.00; Marlow Regional Bank teller $18.75; two big-box retail cashier roles, part-time, $18.50. 'Not a formal survey - just what I'm seeing.'

evidence.source: Talent Acquisition, teller requisition metrics FY2025 vs FY2026
evidence.text: Median time-to-fill: 24 days -> 41 days. Offer acceptance rate: 88% -> 79%. FY2026 offer declines with a recorded reason: 14, of which 9 cite a higher-paying offer elsewhere, 3 cite schedule, 2 other.

evidence.source: Retail Operations, ShiftWise pilot memo (2026-03-20) and vendor contract summary
evidence.text: ShiftWise demand-based scheduling went live 2026-04-13 at 19 of 46 branches, selected by Operations as the highest-transaction-volume branches. These 19 branches hold 214 of 412 tellers (52%). Under ShiftWise, schedules are generated centrally by the Workforce Team and posted 7 days ahead (previously branch managers posted 3 weeks ahead); split shifts allowed. Branch managers at ShiftWise branches cannot edit schedules; they submit change requests to the Workforce Team. The rollout plan, including the planned expansion to every branch, was announced to all tellers at all 46 branches on 2026-03-04. Expansion to the remaining 27 branches is scheduled for 2027-01-11; the contract allows the go-live date to be moved with 30 days' notice at no fee.

Effective 2026-03-02, all 46 branches extend Saturday hours from 9:00-12:00 to 9:00-15:00, and every full-time teller is scheduled for two Saturdays per month (previously one). Applies to all branches regardless of scheduling system.

evidence.source: Teller II, Harbor Point branch (a ShiftWise branch) (interview, 2026-11-06)
evidence.text: "Between the second Saturday and finding out my week only seven days out, I can't line up childcare. Three people on my line left since spring. One went to the credit union - she said the money was better but honestly I think she'd have stayed if she knew her schedule. The other two just quit; I don't know where they went."

evidence.source: Branch Manager, Elm Street branch (not a ShiftWise branch) (interview, 2026-11-07)
evidence.text: "I lost two tellers this year and both went to Lakeshore for about two dollars more. The extra Saturday didn't help - one of them told me that's when she started looking. I've been at this branch six years and I've never had to post a teller job this many times."

evidence.source: Regional VP, Retail Banking, Karen Lindgren (interview, 2026-11-05)
evidence.text: "Pay is part of it, but turnover follows managers. I could name you five branch managers right now who are burning through tellers - I hear the complaints and I see it on branch visits. My proposal: put those five on performance-improvement plans this quarter, and withhold the FY2026 bonus from any branch manager whose branch shows teller turnover above 45%, using the manager field in PeopleCore." Named branches: Harbor Point, Quarry Road, Westgate, Fulton Square, Linden Park.

evidence.source: HR Operations, branch-manager change log FY2026 and PeopleCore data note (2026-10-30)
evidence.text: Seven of 46 branches changed branch manager during FY2026. Among the five branches named by the Regional VP, Harbor Point (new manager 2026-05-18), Westgate (2026-06-08) and Linden Park (2026-07-13) changed managers mid-year. Data note: the PeopleCore 'manager of record' field was loaded from a December 2025 snapshot at migration and has not been updated, so for those seven branches it still shows the previous manager. The branch cost-center code on each separation record is payroll-driven and accurate. HR Analytics estimates a separation report by branch, with corrected manager-of-record dates, can be produced in about 10 business days (by 2026-12-01 if requested now).

evidence.source: State Bankers Association 2026 Compensation & Turnover Survey (turnover summary, released 2026-11-02) and State Department of Labor area statistics
evidence.text: Median teller turnover at participating in-state community banks (n=41): 33% in FY2025, 38% in FY2026. Unemployment rate in the bank's metro areas: 4.4% (Sep 2025) -> 3.5% (Sep 2026). Cedar Hollow did not participate in the 2026 survey.

evidence.source: Payroll, overtime by pay code FY2025 vs FY2026
evidence.text: Teller overtime coded VAC-COVER: 2,140 hours (FY2025) -> 9,760 hours (FY2026). Timekeeping rules allow VAC-COVER only to cover hours of a position with an open requisition, and each entry must carry a valid open requisition number (system-validated). Monthly VAC-COVER hours tracked the count of open teller requisitions throughout FY2026, rising and falling in the same months. All other teller overtime: 3,050 -> 3,180 hours.

evidence.source: CFO, cost note on the proposed teller increase (2026-11-09)
evidence.text: A 15% increase to all teller base pay costs about $2.6M per year including payroll taxes and benefits loading, recurring. Once in base pay it is not practically reversible. FY2027 budget lock: 2026-12-10. A targeted adjustment can be added mid-year through the January structure-review cycle (next one effective 2027-01-18) if approved by 2027-01-05.

hypotheses.text: Below-market teller pay is the primary driver of the rise in teller turnover from 28% to 47%.
The rise in teller turnover is concentrated in the branches of a small number of weak branch managers.
The ShiftWise scheduling rollout raised teller turnover at the 19 branches where it was deployed.
Cedar Hollow's turnover increase is larger than its in-state peers', so regional labor-market conditions alone do not explain it.
The reported rise in turnover is largely a reporting artifact of the December 2025 HRIS migration to PeopleCore.

edges.to: Higher teller turnover at that branch
Rise in Cedar Hollow teller turnover

edges.from: Two-Saturday-per-month requirement and extended Saturday hours (effective 2026-03-02)
edges.to: Rise in schedule-related voluntary teller departures
Increased overtime worked by remaining tellers

actions.text: Approve a 15% across-the-board increase to all teller base pay in the FY2027 budget before the 2026-12-10 budget lock.

Place the five branch managers named by the Regional VP on performance-improvement plans this quarter and withhold the FY2026 bonus from every branch manager whose branch shows teller turnover above 45% according to the PeopleCore manager-of-record field.
Have HR Analytics produce FY2025 vs FY2026 teller separations by branch, with corrected manager-of-record dates, and compare pre- vs post-April 2026 turnover at ShiftWise and non-ShiftWise branches.
Obtain a current teller pay benchmark (e.g., purchase the State Bankers Association 2026 teller pay module) and compare current rates to market before setting any pay adjustment.
Give the vendor notice to hold the 2027-01-11 ShiftWise expansion to the remaining 27 branches until the rollout-status turnover comparison is complete.

evidenceRequests.text: Teller voluntary separations and turnover rates by branch, FY2025 vs FY2026, with corrected manager-of-record dates
Teller turnover before and after April 2026 at ShiftWise vs non-ShiftWise branches
Current market pay data for teller roles in the bank's labor markets (State Bankers Association 2026 pay module)
Customer satisfaction (branch NPS) scores by branch, FY2026
Free-text comments from the FY2026 exit survey
